response: Set up the figure: A is the centre of the circle of radius AP = 7 cm, B is the centre of the circle of radius BP = 10 cm. The common chord PQ is perpendicular to the line of centres AB and is bisected by it at the midpoint M, so PM = MQ = 4 cm. Triangles APM and BPM are right-angled at M. Let AM = x. Then by Pythagoras in triangle APM: AM^2 + PM^2 = AP^2, so x^2 + 4^2 = 7^2, giving x^2 = 49 - 16 = 33, so x = sqrt(33) cm. Let BM = y. In triangle BPM: y^2 + 4^2 = 10^2, so y^2 = 100 - 16 = 84, so y = sqrt(84) = 2*sqrt(21) cm. Since M lies between A and B (the centres are on opposite sides of the common chord), AB = AM + MB = sqrt(33) + sqrt(84) = sqrt(33) + 2*sqrt(21) cm, which is approximately 5.745 + 9.165 = 14.91 cm. Therefore the length of AB is sqrt(33) + sqrt(84) cm, approximately 14.9 cm.
